title: Sunny and the Busy Bee
description: Little Sonny the quokka watches a little bee going about its important, gentle work. A buzzy, warm bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny was sitting near the wattle bush when he heard it.

A low, steady hum. Like the world itself was softly singing.

He looked, and there, moving from flower to flower on the bright yellow wattle blossoms, was a small bee.

It was round and fuzzy and absolutely focused on its work.

Sunny watched as the bee landed on a blossom, tucked in, gathered its treasure, and lifted off again in a smooth little arc to the next flower. And the next. And the next.

It never stopped. It never looked around. It was utterly absorbed in what it was doing.

Sunny thought about that.

The bee didn't seem worried, or hurried, or uncertain. It just knew exactly what to do, and it did it, one flower at a time, until the job was done.

He watched for a long time.

At some point the bee hovered right in front of Sunny's nose, just for a moment, and Sunny held very still. He could see the tiny golden pollen baskets packed on its legs. He could feel the small breeze from its wings.

Then it was gone, back to its work.

Sunny breathed out slowly.

He found a patch of warm ground near the wattle and lay down in the afternoon sun, listening to the soft, steady hum.

It felt like the most peaceful sound in the world.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, busy bee. Goodnight, warm and humming afternoon.
